newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end steady to higher.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed steady to higher on Thursday as the yen's falls against the dollar offset a weaker Chicago market overnight, but the market lacked a clear direction, traders said.
Prices were unchanged to 150 yen higher, with the benchmark March 1998 contract up 40 yen at 16,340 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 38,408 lots.

The market opened mixed as the yen's losses offset the lower Chicago market, traders said. Japanese investors could not find a clear direction throughout the day, and all contracts were traded in a narrow range, they said.
The spot May contract on CBOT Project A was trading at $3.08-1/4 per bushel at 0810 GMT, against $3.08-1/2 at Wednesday's close.
Spot May CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system were at $8.86 per bushel, against $8.83-1/2 at Wednesday's close.
